problem: Source: 'I will tell anybody who asks me questions, this exact tale.' MODERN 'the exact truth' turns Jane's specific threat (to retell this red-room story) into a general claim of truth-telling.
new_text: "How dare I, Mrs. Reed? How dare I? Because it is the truth. You think I have no feelings and that I can survive without a single bit of love or kindness. But I cannot live like that, and you have no pity. I will remember how you shoved me back—roughly and violently shoved me back—into the red room and locked me in there, until my dying day. Even though I was in agony. Even though I cried out, while choking with distress, 'Have mercy! Have mercy, Aunt Reed!' And that punishment you gave me because your wicked boy hit me—knocked me down for nothing. I will tell this exact story to anyone who asks me. People think you're a good woman, but you are bad and hard-hearted. You are the deceitful one!"
